title: Relations, Functions & the Vertical Line Test
subject: Algebra

chunks.text: A relation is any pairing of inputs with outputs, often written as ordered pairs in the form (input, output). It is a general collection of 'this goes with that' pairings.

A function is a special relation in which every input has exactly one output. Like a vending machine where one button always gives the same item, a function gives one predictable output for each input.
The defining rule of a function is that each input has exactly one output. A function never pairs the same input with two different outputs.
In a relation, the set of all inputs is called the domain, and the set of all outputs is called the range.
A function forbids one input from having two different outputs, but it allows two different inputs to share the same output. Repeated outputs are fine; a repeated input with different outputs is not.
A mapping diagram shows inputs on the left and outputs on the right, with arrows connecting each input to its output. For a function, every input has exactly one arrow leaving it.
A relation can be shown four ways: as ordered pairs, as a table of x and y values, as a mapping diagram, or as a graph. Each form has a way to check whether it is a function.
For ordered pairs, a relation is a function if no input (the first number) repeats with a different output. The set {(1, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6)} is a function because all inputs are different.
The set {(2, 7), (4, 9), (2, 1)} is not a function because the input 2 is paired with both 7 and 1, giving one input two different outputs.
The set {(1, 5), (2, 5), (3, 5)} is a function even though the output 5 repeats, because each input has exactly one output and different inputs may share an output.
On a graph, the input is the x-coordinate (horizontal position) and the output is the y-coordinate (vertical position). One input having two outputs means two points stacked at the same x-value.
The vertical line test states that if any vertical line crosses a graph more than once, the graph is not a function. If every vertical line crosses at most once, the graph is a function.
A slanted straight line such as y = 2x + 1 is a function, because any vertical line crosses it exactly once.
A U-shaped parabola such as y = x squared is a function, because a vertical line crosses it at exactly one point for each x-value.
A circle is not a function, because a vertical line through its middle crosses it twice, at the top and the bottom, meaning one input has two outputs.
A vertical line such as x = 3 is not a function, because it overlaps a vertical test line at infinitely many points, giving one input many outputs.
The most common mistake is calling a relation 'not a function' because an output repeats. Repeated outputs are allowed; only a repeated input paired with different outputs breaks the function rule.

To decide if a relation is a function: identify the inputs and outputs, check whether any input repeats, and if one does, check whether it has two different outputs. A repeated input with different outputs means it is not a function.
The single question that settles any function check is: does any input lead to two different outputs? If yes, it is not a function; if no, it is a function.

Functions describe predictable cause-and-effect relationships, such as gas cost depending on gallons, earnings depending on hours worked, or distance depending on time at steady speed, where one input determines one output.

Functions are the backbone of computer programming, where a function takes an input and returns one output. Apps, spreadsheets, and scientific models are built from functions, all using the one-input-one-output idea.
